desc: Seventy-two heavily redacted Navy 'range fouler' reports covering incidents from 2004 to 2021, released through the Navy's FOIA reading room on 13 January 2023, previously classified Secret with distribution limited to the Five Eyes. This is the most important primary-document set on the aviator strand because it proves the encounters were formally reported inside the Navy and then went nowhere. The report on the 14 November 2004 Nimitz incident describes the object as 'solid white, smooth, with no edges ... uniformly colored with no nacelles, pylons, or wings ... approximately 46 feet in length,' names Fravor and Dietrich as aircrew, and then records the disposition in one devastating line: 'Pilots reported the incident through Intelligence Personnel. Reporting terminated at 3rd Fleet, there was no process to share the reporting.' The distribution of the set is itself evidence: no reports at all from 2005-2007, 2009-2012, 2017 or 2020, and nearly 40 percent of the released reports from 2021 alone - a pattern consistent with reporting volume tracking the existence of a channel rather than the existence of the phenomenon.
